The new generality is sound: `IsCurveOver` includes integrality, properness and dimension one; DVR stalks give regularity, without requiring smoothness over an imperfect field. The [conclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/TwoChartModel/ProjectiveEmbedding.lean#L180) is a closed immersion over k into the Proj of a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra, agreeing with [Stacks, Lemma 33.43.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A26).

The removed exact-constants hypothesis needs an actual argument: the construction now uses genus over the full constant field and [generation in positive degrees](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/Pencil.lean#L231). Degree zero can contain extra constants; [surjectivity after homogeneous localization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RingTheory/GradedAlgebra/HomogeneousLocalization/Basic.lean#L162) correctly avoids requiring surjectivity there. Finite-dimensionality and transport to X are retained. [AlgebraicCurves 12B](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#L1115) has no separate tagged Check for projectivity; its actual closed-immersion construction is present and sorry-free. Source and extracted axioms checked; no current-commit rebuild claimed.

The [current statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/QuadraticExtension.lean#L238) now permits fields in any universe. I checked the generalized trace-form, Evens-norm and corestriction interfaces: they still give the degree-two, rank-one specialization of [Kahn, Theorem 2 and Lemma II.2.1](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bruno.kahn/preprints/sw-inventiones.pdf). The trace-zero branch remains hyperbolic; the nonzero-trace branch uses the trace/norm diagonalization, with the (2)∪(d) correction.

Both [Layer 9 Checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants/README.md#L3123) still pass: the [eight unit-square-class tables over ℚ₂(√5)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/WorkedExamples/DyadicSqrt/Five/StiefelWhitney.lean#L174) compute both sides on the exhaustive representatives; the [ℚ₂(i), 1+2i test](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/WorkedExamples/DyadicSqrt/NegOne/Basic.lean#L109) proves the Evens value nonzero and distinguishes the incorrect extra correction. All thirteen supporting theorems remain published and sorry-free. This reassesses the new universe-generalized meaning; no current-commit rebuild is claimed.
Checks distinctness of the eight concrete unit square classes.
Checks that these are precisely the even-valuation square classes.
Checks the representatives are actual valuation-ring units.
Computes corestriction on all eight signed coefficients.
Computes the first invariant of the actual twisted trace forms.
Computes the second invariant of every required dyadic twisted trace form.
Computes the actual Evens norm on every required dyadic unit class.
Checks trace 2 of the actual unit 1+2i.
Checks norm 5 of the actual unit 1+2i.
Computes the sign-calibrating Evens norm as the cup (2)∪(5).
Proves that the calibrated Evens value is nonzero.
Distinguishes the incorrect alternative correction from the nonzero Evens value.
Checks that restriction alone loses the sign distinction.

The universe-generalized [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Clifford.lean#L89) retains the correct convention: full Clifford algebra in even rank, even Clifford algebra in odd rank, and plain discriminant in `sw1Class`. A further primary comparison is [Schulze-Pillot, Proposition 7.28](https://www.math.uni-sb.de/ag/schulze/rsp_lecturenotes_quadraticforms.pdf): its four dimension-modulo-eight cases equal the parities of C(n−1,2) and C(n+1,4). Rank zero has both corrections zero.

The [Layer 8 comparison requirement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants/README.md#L2633) passes with the same two-torsion Brauer normalization. The published [ternary formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/RegularFormClass/Clifford.lean#L282) and [trivial-signed-discriminant specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Clifford.lean#L107) remain sorry-free and check the correction terms. These are the applicable comparison checks; construction of all higher classes is a separate target. The Type u change introduces no new algebraic hypothesis or choice of comparison. Current source and extracted axioms inspected; no current-commit rebuild claimed.
The ternary form computes the actual even-Clifford quaternion class, detecting the nonzero rank-three correction.
On even rank with trivial signed discriminant, the correction reduces to choose(m,2) times (-1) cup (-1).

The [current Type u statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Hasse.lean#L68) still identifies the Hasse invariant with the second Stiefel–Whitney class: the former is the product of quaternion classes over i<j, the latter the sum of their Kummer cups. The generalized Brauer comparison preserves this normalization. This matches [Milnor §3](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/milnorktheoryforms.pdf), whose elementary-symmetric classes map to Galois cohomology; regular-form quotient descent removes diagonalization choices.

The [Layer 8 examples](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants/README.md#L2658) pass: [ranks 0/1, binary and hyperbolic forms](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Class.lean#L245), [square coefficients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Basic.lean#L227), the [two-fold Pfister correction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/Pfister.lean#L90), and [dyadic lines/repeated binaries](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/QuadraticForm/StiefelWhitney/PadicTwo.lean#L78). The ⟨1,a⟩ rows are the existing binary formula with Kummer(1)=0. These published proofs remain sorry-free after the universe change. No new characteristic restriction beyond invertibility of 2 appears; no current-commit rebuild is claimed.
The comparison has the correct empty-product/empty-sum values in ranks zero and one.
The hyperbolic plane has vanishing second Stiefel–Whitney class.
The binary value is exactly the Kummer cup, giving zero for each dyadic form <1,a>.
Square coefficients have zero second class, including all-ones forms.
The two-fold Pfister value includes the minus-one cup correction distinguishing Hasse from Clifford conventions.
The eight dyadic line representatives have the stated first-class table; second classes vanish by the low-rank test.
The eight dyadic repeated-coefficient binary forms have alternating zero/nonzero second classes as specified in the roadmap.

The [current equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Comparison.lean#L268) removes the former Type 0 restriction. Its source remains the actual algebraic Brauer group; its target is continuous H² of the profinite absolute Galois group with discrete separable-closure units and their natural action. This agrees with [Stacks, Theorem 59.61.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03R1). I checked that the generalized explicit-to-continuous comparison still maps cocycle classes to their genuine cohomology classes.

The [7B.3 requirements](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants/README.md#L2434) pass: [crossed-product evaluation, its bundled form and uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Comparison.lean#L287), [coboundary and refinement invariance, finite-quotient compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Inflation.lean#L657), [exhaustion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Inflation.lean#L784), and [split class iff zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Comparison.lean#L119). These current, sorry-free proofs retain the normalization sending the crossed product of c to its inflated class and eliminate dependence on splitting choices. The new universe parameter introduces no characteristic restriction. No current-commit rebuild claimed.
Required normalization on each finite-Galois crossed-product class.
Bundled crossed-product normalization.
Uniqueness eliminates arbitrary equivalence or splitting-field choices.
Inflated continuous class is invariant under changing cocycle representative.
Inflation agrees with the supplier finite-quotient comparison leg.
Compatible splitting-field refinement does not change the inflated class.
Every continuous H² class is represented by a finite-Galois cocycle.
Split-algebra edge case agrees with the zero cohomology class.

The [cochain comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GroupCohomology.lean#L109) identifies `Homₖ(Cₙ(BG;k),M)` with equivariant maps `Cₙ(EG;k) → M`, where `Rep.trivial` makes the coefficient action trivial. The published [pullback](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GroupCohomology.lean#L147) and [descent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cohomology/GroupCohomology.lean#L156) checks pass: they give `f(p_*c)` and recover `f(c)`. Contractibility and freeness make these chains a projective resolution, matching [Brown, §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=13). Thus the Lean isomorphism is ordinary, unreduced Hⁿ(BG;M) ≅ Hⁿ(G,M), for every group, commutative coefficient ring and natural degree. [Stage4.17](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/ClassifyingSpaces/README.md#L238) specifies this cohomology clause without a separate example; Stage4.19 and the finite-cyclic H₂ check concern homology. No additional naturality, local-system or cup-product assertion is made.
The actual comparison used by the declaration sends a base cochain f to c ↦ f(p_*c), fixing the pullback convention in every degree.
The inverse used by the same comparison descends a G-invariant cochain: its value on p_*c is f(c), so the comparison is to ordinary constant-coefficient cochains.
